where: Section 1, Section 2 formula list, worked example 1, exam traps, quiz Q1 and Q4 answers
problem: Powers of ten are printed as plain digits in most places: "4.5–5.5 × 1012", "4–11 × 109", "2.0 × 106", "10-6 L". Read literally these are wrong numbers (1012 instead of 10¹²), and a student skimming on a phone will misread them. Only the Section 1 formula uses a superscript tag.
fix: Use superscripts everywhere: 4.5–5.5 × 10<sup>12</sup> per litre, 4–11 × 10<sup>9</sup> per litre, 150–400 × 10<sup>9</sup> per litre, 2.0 × 10<sup>6</sup>, 10<sup>−6</sup> L, 4.0 × 10<sup>12</sup> per litre.

problem: The stated formula uses V in µL, but the example plugs in V = 0.2 mL. The arithmetic is right, but the mismatch with the formula invites unit mistakes in the exam.
fix: Write step 2 as V = 0.2 mL = 200 µL, and either use the µL form of the formula or say plainly that working in mL gives cells per mL, which the next step converts to litres.

where: Section 1, dilution step and the formula that follows
problem: "D is often 1:200" can be read as D = 1/200, yet the formula says multiply by D. A student who substitutes 0.005 gets a count 40,000 times too small.
fix: Add one line: for a 1:200 dilution D = 200 (1 part blood made up to 200 parts); D is always the number you multiply by, and it equals the dilution ratio written after the colon.

problem: Listing platelet, red cell and white cell pulses in one pass of the same unlysed sample suggests all three are counted together. In whole blood white cells are about one per thousand red cells, so the white count is taken on a separate aliquot after the red cells are lysed.
fix: Add: in whole blood the few white cell pulses sit on a huge red cell background, so the white count is made on a sample whose red cells have been lysed; the red cell and platelet counts come from the unlysed aliquot.

problem: The cross-reference "as in 3.1" is plain text, so it does not link to the earlier chapter the way other cross-references do.
fix: Replace with a link to that chapter, for example as in 3.1.
